Changed answer from Yes to No. RoBERTa is used as part of the semantic correctness evaluation pipeline (SeCA metric), but this is an automated model-based metric, not an LLM-as-judge scenario where an LLM evaluates outputs after generation. LLM-as-judge specifically refers to using large language models as evaluators, which this paper does not do.

overall_notes: The extraction was generally accurate. Main issues were: (1) Question 3 had incorrect 'Yes' answer - paper uses automated model-based evaluation (RoBERTa classifier) but not LLM-as-judge; (2) Some background tasks were incorrectly included as main tasks; (3) Minor normalization needed for consistent naming. The paper focuses on structured graph generation using NLG techniques with comprehensive evaluation including both automatic metrics and human evaluation.
